newsitem.title: SPAIN: Italy PM calls Bossi breakaway a joke, but warns....
newsitem.headline: Italy PM calls Bossi breakaway a joke, but warns....

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Tuesday dismissed as a noisy joke a "declaration of independence" by the separatist Northern League but threatened a sharp crackdown if it led to illegal actions.
In a breakaway bid branded a fiasco by Italian media, League leader Umberto Bossi declared a "Republic of Padania" on Sunday for a region covering the powerhouse areas of Italy's economy.

"The Italian people have the sense of humour needed to interpret this political event," Prodi told a news conference after talks with Spanish Prime MinisterJose Maria Aznar in the seaside city of Valencia.
But asked what would happen if Bossi tried to set up an independent military force for his self-declared territory of Padania, Prodi replied:
"I have seen a lot of proposals that have been withdrawn in the end...but if they do anything outside the law the government reaction will be strong, rigorous and immediate."
Prodi confirmed his government's intention of pressing on with federal reforms, saying they had already been underway before Bossi's highly-publicised declaration.
"I have always been a federalist, well before Bossi," he said. "We will press ahead with the reforms we presented in our electoral programmes".
Prodi's centre-left government is working on two packages of laws giving local authorithies greater powers of administration and taxation.
